newsitem.title: USA: N.J. Transport Fund clarifies FY '98 bonding plans.
newsitem.headline: N.J. Transport Fund clarifies FY '98 bonding plans.

text.p: A New Jersey transportation official said Tuesday the state has not yet decided whether a $200 million cash windfall will translate into more bonding in fiscal 1998 by the Transportation Trust Fund Authority.

David Brown, a spokesman for Department of Transportation, said in a telephone interview that officials are still considering whether the extra spending planned for the fiscal year beginning July 1 will require more bonds.
In an earlier interview, Brown said the state did not expect more bonding to result.
The trust fund normally spends about $700 million annually, but in fiscal 1998 the figure will jump to $900 million, boosted by unexpectedly low debt service payments on outstanding debt.
"We've not decided where the $200 million will break down between cash and bonds," Brown said. "That's being decided right now."
